text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto refused to resign and said she had rejected IMF demands for a defence spending cut. "Conspiracies against my government have been hatched but let me declare that I would not tender resignation under any circumstances," she told the National Assembly (lower house).

- The government has moved a constitutional amendment bill in the National Assembly to make accountable public servants, including the president, prime minister, and members of the superior judiciary and civil and military bureaucracy.
- The envisaged investment at the Karachi Export Processing Zone rose 67 percent to $35 million in 1995/96 (July-June) from $11 million in 1994/95.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange payments exceeded the staggering figure of $4.2 billion in 1995/96 for servicing and amortisation of long-, medium- and short-term liabilities.
- More than a dozen students and a policeman were injured in a clash involving protesting students at Peshawar University.
- Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar flew to Mazar-i-Sharif on Sunday in a new attempt to broker peace talks between warring Afghan factions.
- A two-member mission of Moody's Investors Service headed by Ms Lindow, starts a review of Pakistan's economy today.
- Bhutto has presented a list of 250 loan defaulters for expeditious recovery of loans.
- Pakistan agreed to provide a temporary operational and maintenance base for the Afghan state airline Ariana.

- The IMF will release the suspended tranche of the standby loan in early November as the government has agreed to introduce economic reforms prescribed by the IMF. A mini-budget in line with IMF conditions will be announced on Tuesday by State (central) Bank of Pakistan governor Muhammad Yaqub.
